problem_type: Vendor model indexes can delegate to another index document instead of listing model pages directly
symptom: The online APIMart model radar cannot discover models after the root llms.txt began pointing to _llms/en/api-manual.md.
direct_cause: The radar parses only direct model links from the first fetched document and treats a delegated index link as an ordinary non-model page.
class_root: The discovery boundary has no bounded delegated-index traversal contract, so any vendor can reorganize an index without a deterministic parse failure or cycle guard.
affected_population: Future vendor indexes that split locale, category, or manual indexes into delegated documents

external_sources.purpose: Observed the root index delegating to _llms/en/api-manual.md.

invariants: A vendor index may delegate to a bounded number of same-vendor index documents.
Delegated-index cycles and empty terminal catalogs fail visibly instead of reporting zero new models.
Model pages remain the only entries emitted into the normalized catalog.
generality_proof: Both online fetches and offline fixtures use the same bounded index-expansion boundary, so direct, split, localized, and cyclic vendor indexes receive one deterministic policy before model normalization.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Fetch and expand direct or delegated vendor indexes with same-origin, depth, cycle, and non-empty-result checks.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: All online vendor documents pass through loadVendorIndex before parsing.
Offline source documents use the same expansion and parse boundary, making the failure reproducible without network access.

recurrence.reason: Documentation generators commonly split indexes by locale/category, and another vendor or a future APIMart reorganization can reproduce the same empty-discovery failure.
same_class_scan: Inspected parseApimart, parseKie, online fetch, and offline input paths in scripts/model-radar.ts.
Inspected scripts/model-radar.test.ts for direct-index-only fixtures and missing cycle/empty-index coverage.

prevention.invariant: Every vendor index resolves to a non-empty terminal model catalog through bounded same-vendor traversal.
prevention.failure_mode: Traversal rejects cycles, excessive depth, cross-vendor delegation, fetch failure, or a terminal zero-model result with a visible error.
prevention.strategy: Move document loading and delegated-index expansion ahead of vendor parsing so no caller can silently interpret a routing document as a model catalog.

legacy_paths.rationale: The direct-only fetch path is replaced by the bounded shared loader; no fallback preserves silent empty discovery.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant belongs to Nomi's deterministic index loader and does not depend on a parser package version.

migration: No persisted user data changes. Existing radar baselines remain untouched until the user reviews the new report.
residual_risks: A future vendor may publish a non-Markdown or JavaScript-rendered index, which requires a separately reviewed loader rather than weakening this contract.
